messages:
sam: Quick follow-up from the token-mesh RFC — we need to nail the safety-handoff interface between admission and the abuse detector. Putting up a couple tradeoffs and a proposal.

anna: tl;dr? what's the main decision we need to make now?

sam: Two things: 1) sync vs async handoff of client reputation (i.e., block/score) at admission time, 2) whether the safety service should return a hard deny or a soft-score + suggested penalty to the admission layer.

mike: sync deny is easiest for correctness (no race) but adds median latency. we're talking ~3-8ms extra per admission call depending on placement. that matters for short chat turns.

jess: async is lower latency but we risk accepting a request that should've been blocked. We already have prefix-caching for KV — could we do eventual-catch with a short rollback (evict response) pattern?

sam: option sketches:
- SYNC-HARD: admission calls safety API, gets allow/deny. Simple, deterministic. Cons: latency, scaled QPS to safety cluster.
- SYNC-SOFT: safety returns score + penalty, admission applies local policy. Good for fast config, slightly more complex policy logic.
- ASYNC-LETTING: admission proceeds, safety publishes signals to token-mesh; downstream probes evict/pro-rate later. Lower p99 but weaker prevention guarantees.

anna: we should also consider multi-region routing. If admission is in us-west and safety is in us-east, sync hits cross-region latency. Do we replicate compact signals to edge caches?

mike: replication idea: maintain a small LRU per-edge of recent abuse tokens + TTL. Admission first checks local cache; on miss, fall back to sync call to safety. That reduces average latency for hot abusers.

jess: ack. cache correctness question: how long should TTL be? too long -> stale allow; too short -> cache misses. propose conservative 30s default, adjustable per-client severity.

sam: agreed. Also need API shape. Proposal for SYNC-SOFT endpoint:

``` 
POST /v1/safety/assess
{ "client_id": "cid-123", "request_hash": "sha256...", "context": { ... }}

Response:
{ "score": 0.87, "action": "throttle", "penalty_ms": 250, "confidence": 0.92 }
```

Admission semantics: if action == deny -> reject immediately. If throttle/penalty -> admission can inject token-delay or soft-queue. Score + confidence used for metrics and dynamic thresholds.

mike: love the structured response. Implementation note: keep action enums small (allow, throttle, deny, escalate). avoids ambiguity.

anna: for ASYNC-LETTING mode, can we emit a deterministic request id so safety can reference and if it decides to revoke, it can send a revoke command to a cancellation API?

sam: yes, we already have request_id in our frontdoor. Revoke pattern is viable but requires idempotent downstream sidecars and user-visible transparency (we shouldn't silently drop accepted requests without tracing).

jess: operational concerns: safety will be a hotspot. we should add a rate-limiter/gating layer (circuit-breaker) on the safety API so admission can fallback gracefully (e.g., degrade to SYNC-SOFT LOCAL heuristics).

mike: telemetry: we need token-level counters: assessments, denies, revokes, false-positive reports. Also histogram of additional latency for sync calls broken down by region.

sam: decision proposal (vote): default to SYNC-SOFT with edge LRU cache + per-region replica async fanout. Revoke API available for high-confidence revocations (used sparingly). Circuit-breaker on safety with local heuristics fallback. TTL default 30s.

anna: +1 for SYNC-SOFT default. prefer TTL 20-30s depending on client churn; allow overrides per tenant.

mike: +1, but push for an opt-in SYNC-HARD for enterprise tenants that need deterministic blocking with SLA on latency (they accept higher p50).

jess: +1. add a soft rollout plan: start with lab traffic, then canary to 10% ingress, collect metrics (p50/p95 latency, denied rate, revokes, customer complaints).

sam: rollout checklist:
- API proto on safety (SYNC-SOFT) + schema
- edge LRU impl in admission + config
- circuit-breaker + local heuristic fallbacks
- telemetry dashboards and alert rules
- revoke API and audit log
- enterprise opt-in SYNC-HARD path

ops-bot: scheduled: canary pipeline queued for branch token-mesh/sync-soft-canary in 15m. :hourglass:

anna: I'll write the API proto and a short adaptor for admission this afternoon. assigning: anna -> proto, mike -> edge cache, jess -> circuit-breaker + rollout playbook, sam -> telemetry & revoke audit schema.

sam: cool. I'll post a short RFC update summarizing this thread and link to the proto PR once anna has it. if anyone has objections speak now, else i'll treat this as accepted and start the canary plan.

mike: one more thought: for soft scores we should expose a 'reason_code' token so support can explain decisions to customers (and for manual appeals). small string code keys.

jess: good call.

sam: ok noted. thanks all. finishing RFC update in ~1h.
